ambiguities.evidence: Equation (3.15) divides by norm2(hat_Z_k hat_y_k), but neither that definition nor the use in (C.7) states a separate nonzero-denominator assumption (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, anchor: equation (3.15); PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, anchor: equation (C.7)).
ambiguities.impact: The exact bracket remains valid, but the relative correction estimate and the approximate-equality conclusion require an interpretation or exclusion of the zero-product case.
ambiguities.issue: rho_A^R can be undefined when norm2(hat_Z_k hat_y_k) = 0.

ambiguities.evidence: Section 2 defines several 2-norm/Frobenius-based condition numbers and says the paper often writes simply kappa when the context does not require differentiation (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, anchor: condition-number notation); equation (C.7) uses unqualified kappa(A) (PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, anchor: equation (C.7)).
ambiguities.impact: This does not affect the exact triangle bracket, but an exact formalization of its conditional smallness consequence must choose the intended condition number or retain it abstractly.
ambiguities.issue: The condition-number norm hidden by kappa(A) is not fixed locally.

contract_plain_english: The stored product hat_Z_k hat_y_k and the analysis-only product tilde_Z_k hat_y_k differ by exactly Delta Z_k^(2)hat_y_k, so the latter's 2-norm is at most the former's 2-norm plus the correction's 2-norm, with the matching lower triangle bound also displayed. Only after bounding that correction by c(n,k)u_a kappa(A)rho_A^R and assuming it is small does the paper call the two product norms approximately equal (PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, anchor: equations (C.7)-(C.8) and following text).

source_evidence.observation: For j <= k, the stored vector is hat_z_j = fl(M_R^-1 hat_v_j). Matrix-product rounding is represented by fl(A M_R^-1 hat_v_j) = (A + Delta A^(j))hat_z_j, with |Delta A^(j)| bounded componentwise by c(n,k)u_a|A|. The proof defines tilde_z_j = hat_z_j + A^-1 Delta A^(j)hat_z_j and tilde_Z_k = [tilde_z_1,...,tilde_z_k], so that fl(A M_R^-1 hat_v_j) = A tilde_z_j.

The matrix-product correction is Delta Z_k^(2) = [A^-1 Delta A^(1)hat_z_1,...,A^-1 Delta A^(k)hat_z_k], and tilde_Z_k = hat_Z_k + Delta Z_k^(2). The superscript (2) labels this correction component; it is not a square.

Equation (C.7) gives norm2(Delta Z_k^(2)hat_y_k) <= c(n,k)u_a kappa(A)rho_A^R norm2(hat_Z_k hat_y_k). Equation (C.8) gives the exact two-sided triangle bracket norm2(hat_Z_k hat_y_k) - norm2(Delta Z_k^(2)hat_y_k) <= norm2(tilde_Z_k hat_y_k) <= norm2(hat_Z_k hat_y_k) + norm2(Delta Z_k^(2)hat_y_k).

Using u_a kappa(A)rho_A^R << 1 from condition (3.16), the authors combine (C.7) and (C.8) to deduce norm2(hat_Z_k hat_y_k) approximately equals norm2(tilde_Z_k hat_y_k). This approximation is a subsequent conditional consequence, not part of the exact bracket itself.
rho_A^R is defined as norm2(|hat_Z_k||hat_y_k|)/norm2(hat_Z_k hat_y_k), where absolute values are componentwise, and condition (3.16) includes u_a kappa(A)rho_A^R << 1.

The paper uses vector and induced matrix 2-norms and Frobenius matrix norms. The symbol approximately equal and the symbol less-than-or-approximately-equal are used after dropping negligible second-order terms, while c(n,k) denotes an unspecified low-degree polynomial in n and k.

statement.algorithm_linkage: In Algorithm 1 right-preconditioning, each basis vector is first mapped through M_R^-1 and then through A. Appendix C identifies hat_Z_k with the stored results of the former operation and tilde_Z_k with an analysis-only basis absorbing rounding from the latter; equation (C.8) compares their products with the computed least-squares vector hat_y_k (PDF p. 3, printed p. 2, anchor: Algorithm 1 right, lines 6-18; PDF p. 41, printed p. 40, anchor: equations (C.1)-(C.2); PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, anchor: equation (C.8)).
binders: Let 1 <= k <= n and let A in R^(n x n) be nonsingular, as required by the construction using A^-1 in Appendix C (PDF p. 41, printed p. 40, anchor: equations (C.1)-(C.2)).

For j = 1,...,k, let hat_v_j in R^n be a computed Krylov vector, hat_z_j = fl(M_R^-1 hat_v_j), hat_Z_k = [hat_z_1,...,hat_z_k] in R^(n x k), and hat_y_k in R^k be the computed least-squares coefficient vector (PDF p. 41, printed p. 40, anchor: equations (C.1)-(C.2); PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, anchor: equation (3.15)).
Let Delta Z_k^(2) = [A^-1 Delta A^(1)hat_z_1,...,A^-1 Delta A^(k)hat_z_k] and tilde_Z_k = hat_Z_k + Delta Z_k^(2) (PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, anchor: equation (C.5)).
conclusions: The selected upper branch is norm2(tilde_Z_k hat_y_k) <= norm2(hat_Z_k hat_y_k) + norm2(Delta Z_k^(2)hat_y_k) (PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, anchor: equation (C.8), upper inequality).

The same displayed equation also preserves the lower branch norm2(hat_Z_k hat_y_k) - norm2(Delta Z_k^(2)hat_y_k) <= norm2(tilde_Z_k hat_y_k) (PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, anchor: equation (C.8), lower inequality).

Conditionally, if the correction is small as prescribed by (C.7) and (3.16), the paper concludes norm2(hat_Z_k hat_y_k) approximately equals norm2(tilde_Z_k hat_y_k) (PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, anchor: text immediately following equation (C.8)).
constants_and_indexing: The columns and perturbations are indexed j = 1,...,k; Delta Z_k^(2) is an n by k matrix and hat_y_k has k entries (PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, anchor: equation (C.5)).
c(n,k) is an unspecified polynomial of low degree in n and k; no numerical value is supplied (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, anchor: Section 2 definition of c(n,k)).

The superscript (2) on Delta Z_k^(2) distinguishes the matrix-product correction from Delta Z_k^(1), the preconditioner-application correction (PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, anchor: equations (C.4)-(C.5)).
definitions_and_conventions: hat_Z_k is the basis formed from stored computed applications of M_R^-1, whereas tilde_Z_k is a mathematical search-space artifact that additionally absorbs rounding from multiplication by A and is not algorithmically accessible (PDF p. 41, printed p. 40, anchor: discussion following equation (C.2)).
rho_A^R = norm2(|hat_Z_k||hat_y_k|)/norm2(hat_Z_k hat_y_k), with componentwise absolute values in the numerator (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, anchor: equation (3.15)).

The paper's approximation symbol indicates that negligible second-order terms have been dropped; the inequalities in (C.8), by contrast, are displayed as ordinary non-asymptotic inequalities (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, anchor: Section 2 notation; PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, anchor: equation (C.8)).
error_notions: The selected claim bounds the norm of a perturbed basis product; it does not directly bound the solution's normalized forward error (PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, anchor: equation (C.8)).
The associated relative correction measure is controlled through c(n,k)u_a kappa(A)rho_A^R in (C.7) (PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, anchor: equation (C.7)).
exceptional_values: A must be nonsingular because Delta Z_k^(2) is defined using A^-1 (PDF p. 41, printed p. 40, anchor: equation (C.2); PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, anchor: equation (C.5)).

The bracket remains meaningful when hat_Z_k hat_y_k is zero, but rho_A^R and the subsequent relative correction argument then have a zero denominator; the paper does not separately state how that case is handled (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, anchor: equation (3.15); PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, anchor: equations (C.7)-(C.8)).

Overflow, underflow, NaN, and infinity are not discussed explicitly; the stated standard floating-point model presupposes that the modeled operations produce ordinary finite values (PDF p. 5, printed p. 4, anchor: standard floating-point model statement).
higher_order_terms: Equation (C.8) itself is an exact triangle-inequality bracket and contains no omitted term (PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, anchor: equation (C.8)).

The later approximate equality uses the paper's convention of neglecting second-order effects after imposing the smallness condition (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, anchor: approximation convention; PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, anchor: text following equation (C.8)).
hypotheses: The selected upper inequality requires only the exact relation tilde_Z_k hat_y_k = hat_Z_k hat_y_k + Delta Z_k^(2)hat_y_k and the triangle inequality; it does not itself require condition (3.16) (PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, anchor: equation (C.8)).

For the subsequent approximate-equality conclusion, the proof additionally uses norm2(Delta Z_k^(2)hat_y_k) <= c(n,k)u_a kappa(A)rho_A^R norm2(hat_Z_k hat_y_k) and u_a kappa(A)rho_A^R << 1 (PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, anchor: equation (C.7) and text following (C.8); PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, anchor: condition (3.16)).

The surrounding proof inherits the right-preconditioned GMRES setting and the assumptions of Theorem 3.3, but those assumptions are stronger than necessary for the algebraic bracket alone (PDF p. 41, printed p. 40, anchor: opening of Appendix C; PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, anchor: equation (C.8)).
implicit_context: This bracket is an intermediate step in the proof of the conditional attainable-forward-error theorem for right-preconditioned GMRES, not a standalone forward-error theorem (PDF p. 41, printed p. 40, anchor: Appendix C heading; PDF p. 43, printed p. 42, anchor: conclusion of the proof of Theorem 3.3).

The correction Delta Z_k^(2) accounts for matrix-product rounding from applying A; preconditioner-application rounding is already present in the stored vectors hat_z_j and is represented separately by Delta Z_k^(1) elsewhere in the proof (PDF p. 41, printed p. 40, anchor: equations (C.1)-(C.2); PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, anchor: equations (C.4)-(C.5)).
norms: Every norm in equation (C.8) is the Euclidean vector 2-norm (PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, anchor: equation (C.8)).

The surrounding perturbation model additionally uses componentwise absolute-value inequalities and Frobenius matrix norms (PDF p. 41, printed p. 40, anchor: equation (C.1); PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, anchor: equation (C.5)).
numerical_model: The matrix product is modeled by fl(A M_R^-1 hat_v_j) = (A + Delta A^(j))hat_z_j with |Delta A^(j)| <= c(n,k)u_a|A|, where u_a is the unit roundoff used for multiplication by A (PDF p. 41, printed p. 40, anchor: equation (C.1)).
The paper globally adopts the standard floating-point model and assumes its unit roundoffs are substantially below one (PDF p. 5, printed p. 4, anchor: Section 2 opening notation paragraphs).

undebatable_constraints: The upper inequality's middle quantity is norm2(tilde_Z_k hat_y_k), not norm2(hat_Z_k hat_y_k) (PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, anchor: equation (C.8)).
The additive correction is norm2(Delta Z_k^(2)hat_y_k); it is not merely norm2(Delta Z_k^(2)) or a scalar big-O term (PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, anchor: equation (C.8)).
The selected inequality is non-strict and exact once tilde_Z_k = hat_Z_k + Delta Z_k^(2) is fixed (PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, anchor: equations (C.5) and (C.8)).

The smallness assumption u_a kappa(A)rho_A^R << 1 is needed for the approximate-equality deduction, not for the triangle bracket itself (PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, anchor: text around equations (C.7)-(C.8)).
Both branches of the displayed two-sided result must be preserved even though the locator selects its upper branch (PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, anchor: equation (C.8)).
